_meta.title: Input Document Rules — reading the writer-provided .docx files
_meta.purpose: Machine-readable form of 00_Input_WordDoc_Interpretation_Rules.md: which parts of the Writers Template + Media List are real content, which are boilerplate to discard, how the docx is turned into the marker-text intermediate form, and how the media table's columns are recognised. DocxExtractor.js and MediaListParser.js read this file; nothing about input shapes is hard-coded.
_meta.extension_rule: New boilerplate block, new media-table column heading, new red shade, new template signature = a data edit HERE, never a code change.
_meta.precedence: Where 00-PageForge v1 docs disagree with this file or 00_Input_WordDoc_Interpretation_Rules.md, this file wins.

content_start.rule: Real module content starts at the first RED span that opens the document. Detection chain, first hit wins: (1) LITERAL — a bracket fragment whose folded text is exactly one of content_start_fragments; (2) CANONICAL — the first red span whose primary tag resolves to one of content_start_canonicals (Fundamentals templates open with [Fundamental content] / [Fundamental 1 code] / a bare [Title] instead of [TITLE BAR] — verified on ARFUN01, MXFUN03, EXPFUN04); (3) NONE — convert ALL blocks and surface a loud summary warning (PageForge's own fallback). Everything before the start is template front-matter: not interpreted, not converted, not flagged.
content_start.fallback_note: Last chance before the convert-everything fallback: the first RED span whose primary resolves to one of these directive classes opens the document (EXPFUN06 opens at a bare [H1]; ART1005 similar — verified 12/06/26). Front-matter red spans ([tags] rows, damaged brackets) resolve to nothing, so they can never trigger this.
content_start.note: Mid-document, the looser aliases (title/overview/introduction) are headings, never document starts (Tag_Normalisation_Spec.md page-boundary rule 4) — only the FIRST resolving span opens the document.
content_start._fragments_dropdown_note: ROUND 212 (PNR101 family): the new MTK 'Te Aka Taumatua' bilingual template opens at [Content for DROP DOWN MENU] — recognised as a content start so the menu/overview is not trimmed as front matter. Kept in its OWN list (not content_start_fragments) so env REODROPMENU_OFF can revert the whole round faithfully. Measured: the exact bracketed marker exists in EXACTLY PNR101/102/104 corpus-wide.

table_row_boundary_markers._note: ROUND 423 (session 31 — PMT101, the MTK 'Te Aka Taumatua' template written as ONE table). PNR107 and the other 18 MTK modules carry the page / lesson boundary markers ([MODULE CONTENT: PAGE 1], [END OF PAGE], [LESSON N CONTENT], [END OF DROP DOWN MENU]) as PARAGRAPHS between one bilingual table per page; PMT101's writer kept the whole module in one English ║ Māori table and typed those markers as ROWS (the left cell holds the red span, the right cell is empty). IsContentStart reads paragraphs only, so no content start was ever seen and the module was refused as 'no Writers Template' (the 19 Sept intake's one real recognition gap). DocxExtractor.PromoteTableRowMarkers runs first in ModuleResolver.PrepareRun's classify loop (the ONE shared prep choke point — entry parity by construction) and splits a table at every row whose non-empty cells are each exactly ONE red span resolving to a promote_tags canonical and nothing else, emitting the marker as a paraBlock between the two table halves — which turns PMT101's block stream into exactly PNR107's shape; recognition, TrimFrontMatter, the r212 drop-down rescue, the page splitter and the bilingual handlers are all unchanged. MEASURED (outputs/_s31_r1_rowmarkers.cjs over all 545 docx-bearing gold modules, 762 docx incl. the combined WT + Media List files): marker-only rows resolving to these four canonicals exist in EXACTLY PMT101 (9 rows: page 1, end page 4, lesson content 3, end dropdown 1) and in no other document — every other block list is returned as the SAME array, a byte-identical no-op by construction. NOT promoted, deliberately: the [TITLE BAR] ║ [TITLE BAR] rows (19 MTK modules — a content row the bilingual path already reads; 'title bar' is absent from promote_tags), and any row carrying a marker beside other text (ENGS202's page-opener table, the r306 fence). Env ROWMARKER_OFF reverts.

front_matter_blocks_documentation: MTK WRITERS TEMPLATE / WRITERS TEMPLATE title block
Section B — New Content Development header + writer-guidance box
'Adjust the italicised text below' instruction lines
NOTE: this list is documentation only — the [TITLE BAR] boundary above is the actual discard mechanism (the list is never exhaustive).

red_runs.rule: A docx run is RED when its w:color val (lowercased) is in red_hex_values. Consecutive red runs in a paragraph merge into ONE red span, wrapped in the markers below — reproducing the exact intermediate form the validated corpus pipeline was built on.

hyperlinked_tag_runs._link_target_note: THE THIRD FENCE (session 11): a hyperlinked media tag counts only when its link TARGET is a media-file carrier — the hosts measured to carry 590 of the 600 hyperlinked bracket runs (drive 354 / sharepoint 125 / istock 29 / youtube 17 / docs 10 — outputs/_r342_hyperlinked_brackets.log) or a URL with a media file extension. BLL262's `[Audio]` links a tahurangi.education.govt.nz School-Journal resource PAGE (the r279 reading-book family): read as an audio element it let the carousel composer half-build three identical page placeholders where the honest hand-off box stood; it stays the black link line.
hyperlinked_tag_runs._head_words_note: `embed` is deliberately NOT listed (session 11): the only hyperlinked `[embed …]` runs in the corpus are BLL262/BLL263's `[Embed audio book]` — a SharePoint Word-doc link inside a `[Carousel]`, the r279 reading-book family whose honest form is the hand-off box; as a recognised embed element the carousel composer half-built it (the Word doc as an iframe slide + a web page as an image slide). They stay black link lines, the box stays.
hyperlinked_tag_runs._note: ROUND 342 (the autonomous loop, sessions 9 + 11): the BLL phonics writers type a media tag AS A HYPERLINK — `[audio 1]` in the hyperlink blue (1155cc / 3494ba / 0563c1) or black, linked to the sound file on Drive / SharePoint — so it was invisible to the tag detector (only red runs are scanned; round 341 added the near-red band) and shipped as literal text. A run INSIDE a w:hyperlink whose text carries a bracket whose FIRST WORD is in head_words now counts as red. THE FENCE (head_words): those same writers hyperlink EVERY WORD of a phonics word list — [scissors], [wrist], [hedgehog] … ~230 runs, content the gold ships as click-to-hear audioTrigger words — and MXDI201 links [Number and Operations] to a curriculum page; a blanket rule would turn them into red instruction spans. Measured outputs/_measure_r342_hyperlinked_brackets.py (600 hyperlinked bracket runs: audio 226, audiovisual 27, av 12, image 5, video 4, embed 3). THE SECOND FENCE (exclude_words, session 11): a bracket whose words after the head include one of these is NOT a media tag — the XDLS903/904/905 `[Audio Animation N: <sharepoint script> Note this will be repeated across five units]` lines are a CS-produced animation brief (the r233 / CL-0037 class), and routing them to the audio element shipped a bare .mp3 player and LOST the writer's link + note; they stay the literal link line + Writers Note the page already carried. The block a hyperlinked tag run fires on is marked block.hyperTag (a side-channel, never in the text) so MediaBuilder.media can render the words the writer typed inside the same hyperlink (Emit_Templates elements.media_hyperlinked_lead). Strictly additive; the hyperlink target still rides block.links. Env HYPERTAG_OFF reverts.

near_red_tag_runs._note: ROUND 341 (the autonomous loop, session 9): a writer's structural [tag] typed in a NON-STANDARD RED shipped as literal text, because only a run whose w:color is in red_hex_values was ever scanned for tags. Measured over every Writers Template (outputs/_measure_r342_blacktags.py): 96,817 tag brackets are ff0000/ee0000 and 598 sit in a NEAR-RED the list does not name — ed0000 (the HIS NCEA1 writer, 311), fa0000 (ENGFUN02, 165), c00000 (Word's standard Dark Red — the OS* / CED / ARFUN / TEFUN writers, 120), ed1c24, f72b2b — on 30 modules; the gold renders every one of them as its tag (the literal-tag-leak gate's 288 leaks / 46 pages were largely this). THE FENCE (require_bracket): a near-red run counts as red ONLY when it carries a [ or ] — because c00000 is also used for CONTENT (MXFU302 '+ 5 = 9', ENGI401 'tone' / 'pace', ENGS301) and a blanket rule would turn that content into stripped red-text instructions. Strictly additive: no run that is red today changes, no bracket-less run changes. Hue band: r >= min_r AND g <= max_g AND b <= max_b (c0504d — Word's Accent-2 — falls outside on g). The exact list above stays the primary rule. Env NEARRED_OFF reverts.

red_runs.bridge_split_tag_note: ROUND 118 (Chris): Word can split a single uniform-RED [tag] into separate runs and DROP the colour on an interior space, fragmenting ONE tag across two [RED TEXT] marker spans (ANZH304 '[Please embed this journal story (as in ANZHFUN01 phase 2]'). DocxExtractor.#parseParagraph's red-merge loop now BRIDGES a stray non-red whitespace run that sits MID-TAG between two red runs — fires ONLY when the red text so far has an unbalanced '[' (mid-tag) AND the gap run is whitespace-only AND the next run is red, so it reassembles ONE split tag but NEVER merges across real black content (an intentional '[tag: black label]' form) or between two complete tags. The COMMON same-colour split (Word's usual run fragmentation, e.g. '[Tab 1: I'+'ntroduction'+']' -> [Tab 1: Introduction]) was ALREADY merged by the consecutive-red loop — this only adds the whitespace-gap variant. Measured rare (~1-2/60 modules) since the consecutive case dominates; gate-neutral by the tight guard. env REDBRIDGE_OFF reverts.

repair_missing_bracket.rule:
ROUND 174 (Chris, ENGC101-00 'H2] Know:' bug). A writer occasionally drops a square bracket off a tag. TagNormaliser.Parse already repairs the two EDGE forms for CLASSIFICATION (a dangling '[x' with no ']', and a leading 'x]' with no '['), but ~10 OTHER red-span consumers (RenderText, the overview-menu partition, the black-tag strip, InteractiveScanner, ...) read the raw bracket structure and LEAK the literal — ENGC101-00 lost the 'Know' heading and shipped '
H2]
'. This fixes it ONCE at the source: when a CONTENT red span opens with a lone 'x]' (missing the '[') AND the token x resolves to a KNOWN tag by a WHOLE-token match (how in clean_hows — exact / denumbered / denumbered_head; NOT a tag-word EMBEDDED inside writer prose), the missing '[' is inserted into block.text so EVERY downstream consumer sees a well-formed '[x]'. Original case is preserved (RenderText needs it). GENERAL across every tag (lexicon-driven), NOT one module. Measured corpus-wide (outputs/_measure_malformed_brackets.cjs, 197-set): 162 missing-open red spans, ~73 with a clean token across 37 modules; how=embedded correctly rejects all 47 prose/instruction false positives ('that when they click/hover on the letter...' -> audio embedded; 'Please create a dropdown menu for each item]' -> dropdown embedded). The MISSING-CLOSE form ('[hover trigger: ' — 559 occ) is deliberately NOT touched: Parse's dangling repair + RenderText's optional ']?' already absorb it, and it is the deferred split-bracket infoTrigger lever (0 clean render-leaks). env BRACKETFIX_OFF reverts to leaking the literal.

red_runs.collapse_whitespace_only_note:
ROUND 79 (Chris, OSBY201-03): a merged red span whose entire content is WHITESPACE (a writer mis-coloured a space/tab red) is NOT wrapped in a [RED TEXT] marker — it is emitted as a single plain space. Without this, PageSplitter treats the empty marker as a standalone item and FRAGMENTS the paragraph (OSBY201-03 '**Banter is** like playful teasing' split into two

at a red space; corpus-wide 349 such paragraph fragmentations + 1234 cosmetic edge spans). A red span with any non-whitespace content (a real [tag]/instruction) is untouched — the strip fires ONLY on pure whitespace, so it can never drop a tag. Read by DocxExtractor.#parseParagraph; env REDWS_OFF reverts.
red_runs.note: Verified against OSAH401 Writers Template.docx: writers use ff0000 (Word default red) and ee0000. Other colours observed (316757 green, 3494ba blue, 00b050 green, bfbfbf grey) are content emphasis, never tags. New red shade seen in the wild = append the hex here.

table_markers.rule: Docx tables are serialised into the corpus text-table form so the same downstream parsing applies to fresh uploads and the historical parsed corpus.

single_cell._note: ROUND 313 — THE SINGLE-CELL LAYOUT TABLE (the gathering-remainder chain, ticket 3). The r306 rule dissolves a table only when a SPEECH BUBBLE shares it with the [Activity], because that bubble is a reliable proxy for 'one cell holds the character, the other holds the activity'. A ONE-ROW ONE-CELL table needs no proxy: there is no second cell for data to live in, so it cannot be widget data — it is a box the writer drew round an activity, and every builder that meets it reads the whole activity as its data table and declines. MEASURED over all 454 WTs (outputs/_measure_r306_layouttables.cjs re-run corpus-wide, 143 activity-marker tables / 32 modules): the single-cell shape is EXACTLY 8 tables / 6 modules, of which 3 are reo (TRR112 wt9, TRR113 wt28+wt41 — excluded here, the r145/r167 class: reoMode routes tables through the bilingual handlers and that track owns them) and HPFUN903 wt1 is DECLINED by require_explicit_activity_opener (below), leaving FOUR THAT SHIP: ENGI103 wt2 ([Activity 1B]), ENGI400 wt2 x2 ([Activity 2A], [Activity 2C]) and TEDC402 wt3 ([Activity] 1D, the slider). A LIVE-PATH check over all 454 modules (outputs/_r313_firecheck.cjs, which counts the dissolve's OWN run note through ModuleResolver.PrepareRun) agrees exactly — 3 modules, 4 tables — and also confirms the r306 bubble arm still fires on TEDC402 x12 and nowhere else. THE TOOL TRAP THAT COST ENGI103, recorded because it is not specific to this round: the measurement tool skipped every docx whose filename matched /media list/, which also skips the COMBINED '<CODE> Writers Template + Media List.docx' — and that is how 286 of the corpus's 454 modules ship, so the scan was blind to 63% of the library and reported 118 tables / 19 modules on its first run. The filter is repaired in both tools; round 306's own fence measurement was taken with the blind spot in place, so re-measure rather than lean on its numbers before widening anything. ENGI103, HPFUN903 AND THE REST ARE GOLD-VERIFIED: ENGI400's gold ships 2A and 2C as plain blocks inside their activity boxes, ENGI103's gold ships 1B as its own activity box carrying the supervisor note as a 'super-content row' (and ZERO <table> elements in the whole module — before this rule that whole activity was trapped as literal [Activity 1B]/[Activity Heading]/[body] text inside activity 1A's box, with the supervisor note attached to the wrong activity), HPFUN903's gold ships ZERO <table> elements on the whole page, and TEDC402's gold ships 1D as heading + body + quote + slider + journal button with no table anywhere. Today all four ship the writer's whole activity as raw [H3]/[Body]/[quote]/[Button] text inside a <th> in a hand-off box. The r306 fences carry over unchanged (a PAGE_BOUNDARY/SECTION_MARKER span still refuses; the dissolve still runs before the r174 bracket repair, which is what heals TEDC402's 'Activity]' typo). GENERALISING THE OTHER WAY WAS MEASURED AND DECLINED: widening interactive_tags to 'any INTERACTIVE invocation' would fire on 46 tables / 18 modules (the corrected figure, blind spot removed), and the 34 beyond the speech bubble's own 12 are DATA tables that must stay — CEDO501's three 1x4 r305 quiz tables (the very tables r306 named), ENGI400's 6x2 flipCard fronts/backs, TEDC402's own 4x4 flipCard and 5x3/3x3 drag-and-drop option grids, HPFUN901's 3x1 click-drop column and the TRR English|Te Reo pair tables. The interactive tag is not the discriminator; the SHAPE is. REQUIRE_EXPLICIT_ACTIVITY_OPENER — THE FENCE THE ROUND'S OWN WORD-LOSS CHECK FORCED, and the reason HPFUN903 does not ship: its one-cell table contains no opener the writer typed as an activity at all; what makes it 'an activity' is the WIDGET REQUEST '[interactive tool] quiz — tick box yes or no DEV: answers will vary', which merely aliases to the activity tag. Dissolving it did free the seven bike-check questions into a real <ul> — but it also (a) DROPPED the writer's 'DEV: answers will vary' instruction from the page entirely (it survives only in the developer hand-off .txt), which §6 forbids outright, and (b) promoted the first bullet '• Is your seat at a safe height…' into the box's <h3>, a shape the gold ships ZERO times in 2,385 files against Claude's 2 (CEDO502 7_0, a different emitter and a PRE-EXISTING class, recorded not touched). Requiring the bracket to open with the word 'activity' separates that case from ENGI400's '[Activity 2A]' and TEDC402's 'Activity] 1D' structurally rather than per-module, and the TRR112/TRR113 reo cells would have passed it too (they read '[Activity: Embedded] …') — they are held out by the prefix fence instead. HPFUN903 IS A RECORDED FOLLOW-UP, not a permanent decline: it wants the activity-title rule taught that a bullet line is never a title, and the widget-request residue surfaced as a Writers Note, and each of those is a measured round of its own. Env SBSINGLECELL_OFF reverts this arm alone; SBLAYOUT_OFF still reverts the whole rule.

bubble_layout_dissolve._note: ROUND 306 (Chris — free the speech bubble from the page-layout table). A table whose red spans resolve to BOTH an ACTIVITY-family CONTAINER_OPEN marker AND a speech-bubble INTERACTIVE invocation is a PAGE-LAYOUT table, not widget data: the writer laid the activity out in one cell and the character+balloon in the other, and the HUMAN'S OWN ANSWER is to dissolve the table — the finished page ships the two cells as ordinary stacked blocks in reading order (TEDC402-1.0, byte-verified). DocxExtractor.DissolveBubbleLayoutTables turns each cell into one paragraph block (in-cell ' / ' line breaks restored to plain newlines — the r227 soft-break form), BEFORE the r174 bracket repair so a cell's 'Activity]' typo heals too; the [Activity] opener then opens its box and the [Image]+[speech bubble] cell rides the r246 no-table avatar dialect this very module's free-body bubbles already build through. THE FENCE IS MEASURED (outputs/_measure_r306_layouttables.cjs, all 454 modules): activity-marker-alone fires on ~120 tables across ~20 modules that must all STAY tables (bilingual TRR embedded-activity tables, fundamentals accordion/slide tables, CEDO501's r305 quiz tables); BOTH-markers fires on 12 tables, ALL TEDC402. A table carrying any PAGE_BOUNDARY/SECTION_MARKER span never dissolves (an in-cell [End page] reaching the page splitter would churn pagination — ENGS202's page-opener table stays exactly as it is, by design). Env SBLAYOUT_OFF reverts byte-for-byte.

formatting_markers.note: Matches the parsed corpus conventions: **bold**, *italic*, '• ' bullets. Numbered list items keep their literal numbers.
formatting_markers.preserve_leading_space_round67_note: ROUND 67 (Chris, OSBY201-01). A docx splits a styled phrase into its own run, and Word often keeps the inter-word SPACE INSIDE that styled run as a LEADING space (run 'their' has no trailing space; the bold run is ' wellbeing or hauora'). DocxExtractor#parseParagraph wrapped a bold/italic run with blackText.trim() (drops BOTH sides) but only restored the TRAILING space — so the leading space was lost and the words glued ('theirwellbeing…', 'house orwhare'). Measured 326 Claude word+/ glued / 144 pages vs the human's 80 (human ' ' spaced 4709×) — outputs/_measure_boldspace.py. When true, the engine restores the leading space SYMMETRICALLY, only when the run actually had one, so legitimately-glued cases (no leading space) are untouched. Env BOLDSPACE_OFF reverts to the drop form.

front_matter_metadata.rule: The Section-A/B gray info table holds module-specific fields as 'Label: value' paragraphs in the front-matter (before content start). DocxExtractor captures the FILLED ones (a non-empty value after the colon) into run.metadata. This is the ONE place writers add module-specific data inside the otherwise-generic front-matter, so it is mined even though the front-matter is discarded for conversion.
front_matter_metadata.course_is_english_title_backup: The 'Course' value is the module's English course/title (e.g. 'AI Digital Citizenship'). Used as the English title BACKUP when the [TITLE BAR] payload contains only a Te Reo title — the module must NEVER ship with a Te-Reo-only title (verified need: OSAI301's [TITLE BAR] held only 'Kirirarautanga Matihiko AI').
front_matter_metadata.skip_empty_label_rows: A paragraph that is just 'Label:' with no value is the blank template row — never captured.

title_in_code_cell._round321_note: ROUND 321: the TRR1xx MTK front-matter table has no Module Name row; the Module Code cell reads 'TRR108: Ngā Orokati Tuarua – Final Consonants'. The text after the code token (and an optional colon/dash) is kept as metadata.moduleCodeTitle for PageAssembler's MTK title fallback (header.mtk_titles). The moduleCode field itself is unchanged. Env MTKTITLES_OFF.

front_matter_metadata._table_row_fields_note: ROUND 212: the PNR family's front matter carries its metadata as a TABLE ('Module Name | Nga tau: 1 | Numbers: 1'), not 'Label: value' paragraphs. Only the fields listed here are captured from 2-column table rows (label cell | value cell) — deliberately NOT course/moduleCode, so the Course-is-title-backup path can never start firing on modules it never fired on before. Used as the bilingual title source when the module has no [TITLE BAR] payload (PageAssembler; the value pipe-splits reo|english in payload order). Env REODROPMENU_OFF disables the table capture.

paragraph.rule:
ROUND 227 (Chris, the XDLS900 triage — the round-225 recorded lever). A writer's Shift+Enter stores a INSIDE the paragraph; the old w:t-only run extraction silently DELETED it, gluing the text on either side with no separator at all ('…ana”Through perseverance…') — corrupted text, measured 5,999 soft breaks across 357 of 429 WTs. When true, DocxExtractor contributes '\n' at the break's own position in the run text (a with type=page|column stays a page/column break — the page counter is untouched). The downstream machinery already handles multi-line text: renderBlackText emits one

/

  • per line — the MAJORITY gold form for soft-broken black paragraphs (outputs/_measure_softbreak.py: split-p 84 vs same-el-spaced 172-of-which-164-are-EXPFUN03's-house-style vs br 31 vs glued 0 on the top-8 carriers); Utils.Fold collapses \s+ so tag classification is byte-identical; the round-225 proverbSplit boundary rules go dormant (the lines arrive already split). Env SOFTBR_OFF reverts to the glued extraction.

self_closed_skip.rule: ROUND 265 (CHFUN01, 2026-08-05). Word writes an EMPTY paragraph as a SELF-CLOSED <w:p w14:paraId=".."/> (34 of them in CHFUN01, mostly empty table cells inside the Section-A textbox). DocxExtractor.#findClose counted each as an OPEN with no matching close, so the depth ratcheted up and a textbox-carrying paragraph's scan ran to end-of-body — the WHOLE module collapsed into ONE giant block: the front matter leaked into the output, every paragraph boundary was lost (bullets glued, [tags] fused into prose), and IsContentStart never saw the real [TITLE BAR]. When true, a self-closed <w:p .../> contributes NOTHING to the depth scan and is skipped as a top-level block (it has no content). MEASURED corpus-wide (outputs/_measure_selfclosedp.py, exact shipped-semantics replica over all 452 WTs): the block stream changes on EXACTLY 20 modules — 13 giant-ratchet repairs (CHFUN01/04/05/06/07, TRR110, TRR203 — its 'mega-paragraph' was THIS bug — TRR301, HPFUN403, HPFUN902, CEDR302, BLL264, SSOG103) + 7 cosmetic BLL boundary shifts; every selfP=0 module is untouchable BY CONSTRUCTION. Env toggle: SELFCLOSEP_OFF reverts to the ratchet.

math.rule: ROUND 346 (the autonomous loop's session 12, 2026-09-16 — Chris's D10-7, Option A: MathML, the gold's form and the one that renders in MTK; KB delta: 05A 'MathJax / Equations' → MathML is the shipped form). A Word equation is not a w:r run — it lives in an <m:oMath> beside the runs of a w:p (329 equations across 12 Writers Templates, every one inline beside runs; not one <m:oMathPara> in the corpus — outputs/_measure_r346_omml.py), so the run walk never saw it and every equation silently vanished from the page. Now each <m:oMath> is converted by OmmlMathml (the V1.5 pageforge-site/js/omml-to-mathml.js port; vocabulary r/t, f, sSup, sSub, d, rad = the corpus's whole OMML vocabulary, the rest of the grammar implemented anyway and an unknown element recursed as <mrow>, never dropped) and replaced IN PLACE by a synthetic black run carrying a private-use sentinel (U+E010 <id> U+E011) that flows through every text path — tag classification, coalescing, the emoji strip, the hover sentinels U+E000/E001, the typed-number list — unchanged; PageAssembler's final post-pass swaps the sentinel for the <math xmlns=…> markup (bare — the gold's 1873 : 105 inline : 70 block majority; MathJax renders it either way) and adds body_class_token to the <body> class of every page that carries a <math> (the gold's per-page form, 0.92 precision); the hand-off .txt gets the same swap. Verifier reference/tests/_verify_math.cjs: per module, the docx <m:oMath> count == the pages' <math> count, every <math> page carries mathJax, no sentinel leaks (defect 0). Env MATHML_OFF reverts byte-for-byte (the equations vanish again).

text_normalise.rule: ROUND 241 (Dev-Feedback R4, E1 — SCCH302's 'AI marker' NBSP; the r227 extractor seam). Word documents carry invisible whitespace characters the writer never intended as content: the NON-BREAKING SPACE U+00A0 (autocorrect/paste residue — the developer flagged it as an 'AI marker'; SCCH302's own [TITLE BAR] Te Reo carries 5) and the ZERO-WIDTH characters U+200B/U+200C/U+200D/U+FEFF (paste residue from web sources). MEASURED corpus-wide (round 241, live docx scan): NBSP 15,198 occurrences across 416 of 429 WTs; zero-width 124 occurrences across 22 WTs; the converted corpus SHIPS 2,108 literal NBSPs on 298 pages while the gold library ships effectively none (37 literal on 7 pages — the human's ~1,026 ' ' ENTITIES on ~45 pages are deliberate layout, not writer residue). When enabled, DocxExtractor normalises each run's decoded w:t text at extraction (the same seam as the r227 soft-break fix): U+00A0 → a plain space (nbsp_to_space), and the zero-width set is deleted (strip_zero_width). GRANULARITY SAFETY (the r227 red-run trap): an NBSP-only run stays a non-empty whitespace piece (same trim()/Fold behaviour before and after — JS whitespace includes U+00A0), so red-span merging is untouched; a run the zero-width strip EMPTIES drops out exactly like an always-empty run — the tags gate (9557/9557 spans, REAL 0) is the authoritative granularity detector and is proven unchanged in the round's probes. Tag CLASSIFICATION is inert by construction either way (Utils.Fold collapses \s+, and \s matches U+00A0). Env NBSP_OFF reverts the whole normalisation (NBSPs and zero-width characters flow through to the page again).

answer_marks.rule: ROUND 309 (Chris — the r306 follow-through chain ticket 3, WHY_UNBUILT__dropDown reasons 4+5). The extractor kept the writer's RED text and nothing else; writers ALSO mark the correct answer of a quiz with a yellow HIGHLIGHTER (<w:highlight>, never read before this round) or with GREEN text (00b050 — distinct from the template's own guidance green 316757, which stays ignored; the two greens were conflated in the old red_runs verification note and are split by this round's measurement: OSAH401 uses 00b050 for exactly its announced answers). This channel records those marks as a SEPARATE side-channel — block.marks = [{text, kind: 'hl'|'green'}] on a paragraph block (consecutive same-kind marked runs merge, a pure-whitespace gap bridges), and block.cellMarks (rows-aligned per cell) on a table block — WITHOUT touching block.text by a single byte, so tag granularity, red-span structure and every existing consumer are byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION (the tags gate 9557/9557 is the canary). 'white' highlight is template guidance chrome (the OS-family 'Refer to How to Merge Content.pdf' lines) and never a mark. NO consumer acts on a mark without its own fence: round 309's dropDown reading requires the writer's own ANNOUNCEMENT ('Correct answers highlighted' / 'Correct answers in green') in the same bundle — measured essential, because highlight is also used editorially (TRR109's whole-paragraph highlights) and green marks the OPTIONS themselves on OSAI101, where reading it as an answer would ship a WRONG quiz. Env ANSMARK_OFF reverts the channel (no marks recorded, every consumer dormant).

render_text.rule:
ROUND 104 (Chris, OSAH501-00 whakataukī ':' bug). TagNormaliser.RenderText extracts the ORIGINAL-CASE text a writer left OUTSIDE the brackets of a tag span (e.g. '[H1] INTRODUCTION' -> 'INTRODUCTION'). When the writer glues a STRAY PUNCTUATION character to the tag and nothing else ('[whakatauki]:' -> ':'), that residue is NOT content — it is writer noise — yet it leaked downstream as an embedded LEAD (the whakataukī box rendered a spurious '

:

' before the proverb). When true, a RenderText result that contains NO letter or digit in ANY script (Unicode \p{L}/\p{N} — macrons ā/ē/ī/ō/ū count as letters, so te reo is never dropped) is treated as EMPTY (''), so the noise vanishes and any '|| blackAfter' fallback chain falls through to the real content. ROBUST + GENERAL: handles any erroneous glued character (':', ';', '-', '.', '|', '(', ']', '*', '…') across EVERY tag and EVERY RenderText caller, not just whakataukī. CONSERVATIVE: a residue with even one letter/digit (a real embedded title/label) is untouched. Measured corpus-wide (outputs/_measure_strayleadpunct.cjs): 42 punctuation-only leads across 26 modules; the human renders none of them. Env STRAYLEAD_OFF reverts to leaking the punctuation residue.

emoji_strip.disclosure: Emoji have been removed from this content per the no-emoji rule. Ticks and crosses are retained.
emoji_strip.rule:
ROUND 234 (Chris — Change Ledger CL-0051, 16 Jul; the FIRST CL-0001/constraint-1 exception permitting deletion of writer characters). Emoji are stripped from rendered writer content: ListsAndRuns.EmojiStrip runs as a FULL-PAGE POST-PASS (the r213 LinkTextDisplay seam — after OmitPlaceholderResidue + TidyDeveloperNotes, before LinkTextDisplay/Indent, stopping at the acks block), so every emitter is covered uniformly and NO pre-render machinery can be disturbed: tag classification, the ✅-glued [TITLE BAR] fences (OSSC301/r230), the r192 ✅[Tile] delimiters, the r169 title splits and the 🔴 red-run sentinels all operate on block text long before this pass — post-pass placement makes them untouchable BY CONSTRUCTION. SCOPE = Unicode Extended_Pictographic grapheme CLUSTERS (base + VS15/16, skin tones U+1F3FB-FF, ZWJ sequences, keycap marks; regional-indicator flag pairs; a keycap digit keeps its digit and loses only the dressing), matched cluster-whole so a VS16 is NEVER orphan-stripped off a kept tick. 'exempt' = the ledger's ticks & crosses VERBATIM (✓✗✘ are not Extended_Pictographic and could never match anyway — listed for fidelity). 'exempt_extensions.maths_operators' = the ONE measured extension (✖➗➕➖ — meaning-bearing operators in maths content; gold keeps ✖ x12; ✖ is a cross by form, the ledger's own ☑ inclusion proves heavy/box variants count). 'arrow_map' = EP arrow emoji become PLAIN arrows instead of deletions (gold's own treatment — TEDC402 ships the writer's 'input🡪process🡪output' as 'input→process→output'; meaning kept, emoji removed). OUT OF SCOPE by the Unicode property (measured decisions, round-234 census outputs/_measure_emoji.py): the checkbox/ballot family ☐☒□🗹 (bilingual checklists + printable tick-sheets — 671 visible; the r212 checklist→bullet stays the reo-menu machinery), 🖵 phonics sound-boxes (BLL147), 🡪 (TEDC401 gold keeps it), plain →←, typographic ►●◦, private-use chars — none are emoji per Extended_Pictographic. CLAUSES: a run of 2+ consecutive PLAIN

lines each PREFIXED by a would-be-deleted cluster becomes ONE

    of
  • (the lead cluster dropped; measured 23 runs — CEDT104 '🎵Sing/🎵Do/🎵Feel', ARFUN02's instrument list; an exempt-led line like '✅ I did it.' never joins a run and stays a

    ); a LONE prefixed line stays a

    ; in-prose clusters are removed with spacing normalised (doubled spaces collapsed, space-before-punctuation healed — 'earn a star ⭐️.' → 'earn a star.'); a plain

    the strip EMPTIED is dropped whole (drop_emptied — ARFUN02's 31

    🤔

    ; gold ships zero; a PRE-EXISTING empty

    is never touched). DISCLOSURE: ONE visible note per affected page at the first removal, ledger wording verbatim in 'disclosure', emitted through NotesAndComments.redFlag (kind diagnostic → 'Red Flag:' prefix, red+bold, class cv2-note = gate-excluded by construction; NOTESCHEME_OFF legacy form applies to it like any note); a first removal inside the header/menu relocates the note to the top of the body (the r203 no-comments-in-menu rule). CONTAINMENTS (all measured): cv2-interactive placeholder subtrees (6,949 chars — the developer's verbatim hand-off, the r201/r213 class), cv2-note/cv2-comment payloads (writer quotes stay verbatim), the acks block (gold keeps oEmbed video titles verbatim + the converter's own ❗ ack-todo markers are functional chrome),

module_code_detection._doc: ROUND 421 (the autonomous loop's session 30 Round 4). ModuleResolver.DetectModuleCode reads the module code with one regex — 2-6 letters + 2-4 digits (+RR) — over the filenames, then the first front-matter paragraphs. Four intake codes fall outside it: CHWHA / GEWHA (no digits), ANZHFUN05 (seven letters), PWYWHA1 (one digit — and its front matter mentions PWY1000, so it converted AS PWY1000). Their builds shipped as MODULE_0_0.html / PWY1000_0_0.html and the round-408 registry rows mined for exactly these codes were never reached (global defaults instead). registry_token: between the filename regex and the front-matter regex, each filename's LEADING token (split on `separators`, upper-cased) that is a key of Module_Structure_Index.module_meta is a candidate — a code the regex cannot shape still resolves when the corpus registry knows it. The regex keeps precedence (an unchanged path for every module it already names); the front-matter regex stays the last resort. Env CODEREG_OFF restores the regex-only detection.

wt_page_tracking.rule: Each content block is stamped with the Writers Template page it sits on, counted from: w:lastRenderedPageBreak elements (Word's own pagination record), explicit w:br type='page', and w:pageBreakBefore paragraph properties that are TRUE (bare element or val='1'/'true' — Google-Docs exports write val='0' meaning NO break; never count those).
wt_page_tracking.reliability_note: Google-Docs-exported templates (verified on OSAH401) carry NO usable pagination records, so page numbers may stay at 1. The acks lesson-mapping therefore treats page records as only ONE evidence source — see media_item_lesson_mapping below.
wt_page_tracking.page_records_usable_when: the counted page total is at least min_pages_for_trust

media_item_lesson_mapping.rule: Mapping a media item to its lesson (for acksLesson grouping) uses the strongest available evidence, in order. Guessing is banned; every interpolated or fallback placement is reported in the conversion summary.
order: 1. CONTENT MATCH — the item's normalised URL (or unique asset ID) appears in exactly one lesson's content blocks → that lesson.
2. PAGE RECORDS — when the WT docx has usable pagination (see wt_page_tracking), the item's WTPg No. falls in one lesson's page span → that lesson.

3. NEIGHBOUR INTERPOLATION — media lists run in page order; an unmatched item between two items mapped to the SAME lesson belongs to that lesson. Between different lessons → the earlier lesson, and the placement is reported in the summary.
4. FALLBACK — remaining items go to the first content group, each reported in the summary (never dropped).

unsupported_pathways.where: any paragraph before content start, folded
unsupported_pathways.label: MTK / Te Reo Rangatira (TRR) bilingual template
unsupported_pathways.action: Do not convert. Surface a clear visible notice in the conversion summary: this template follows a separate bilingual pathway (paired reo/eng elements) and must not be force-fitted through the standard rules.
unsupported_pathways.note: The 'MTK WRITERS TEMPLATE' heading ALSO appears in standard templates' front-matter (verified on OSAH401), so the signature alone is not enough — the module code prefix must match too.

media_table.identify_rule: A docx table is THE media table when its first row matches at least min_header_matches of the column families below (folded, punctuation-insensitive). In a combined WT+media-list docx the media table is located anywhere in the document and is excluded from content conversion.

strip_markers._note: ROUND 372 (the autonomous loop's session 23, Round 3, 2026-09-18). The media-table cell cleaner also strips the extractor's **bold** / *italic* asterisk markers before the header fold and the row parse (never an underscore — a URL character: the first probe collapsed Pita_Sharples in a Wikimedia link). Measured through the live extractor over all 416 modules (outputs/_s23_boldheader.cjs): exactly four modules — BLL120 (185 rows; every data cell bold too), BLL121, BLL122, BLL123 — typed the header cells bold, so the exact alias match never fired and the module parsed NO media list at all (their [Item N] references, iStock filenames and acks entries stayed unresolved; the table rendered as a kept <table> on the last lesson page). A marker the extractor added is never a header word or a URL character; the gold's acks never carry one. Env MLMARKERS_OFF = the pre-round cleaner, byte-identical.

example_row.rule: Drop any data row matching the template's worked example: item_no folded equals 'example', OR the description contains an example_signature.

discard_rows.reminder_rows: Drop any full-width/merged row (a row with a single spanning cell) and any row whose first cell starts with 'reminder' — these are writer guidance, not items.
discard_rows.header_row: The first (header) row itself is never an item.
discard_rows.empty_rows: Drop rows where every cell is blank.

media_table.hyperlinks: URLs are usually Word hyperlinks: the visible cell text may be truncated or decorative — ALWAYS resolve the run's w:hyperlink r:id against word/_rels/document.xml.rels (TargetMode='External') and prefer the rel Target over visible text.
media_table.description_caution: The Description column is the writer's own wording — NEVER use it as an acknowledgement {Title} for stock assets (Acks_Formats.json title_authority).

input_shapes.separate: Two files: one docx containing a [TITLE BAR] (the WT), one docx whose only substance is the media table (the media list).
input_shapes.combined: One docx containing both the [TITLE BAR] content and a media table.
input_shapes.classification_rule: Per uploaded file: has content_start fragment → WT; has media table but no content start → media list; has both → combined. Neither → red flag in summary (unrecognised document). ROUND 424: a docx with no content start whose table opens with the two-cell header 'Section heading | Text/Activity' is the ACTIVITY-TABLE dialect (activity_table below) — a Writers Template in a different dialect, recognised as the WT and, until the adapter ships, refused BY NAME instead of falling into 'unrecognised'.
input_shapes.no_media_list: If no media table is found anywhere, still generate the acknowledgements block (standing items + per-lesson designer-media check lines) and surface a clear summary warning.

activity_table.label: Activity-table Writers Template (the XOTP reader family — a 'Section heading | Text/Activity' table, no red tags)
activity_table.action: Recognised as a Writers Template in the ACTIVITY-TABLE dialect: the left cell of each row (Overview / Introduction / Online book / Questions / a bare activity number …) carries the structure that red tags carry in the standard template. The adapter that turns that table into PageForge's tag stream is not enabled yet (input_shapes.activity_table.adapter) — nothing converted; see 00-NEW_NEW_NEW/_SPEC__XOTP_Activity_Table_Template.md.

adapter._shipped_inert: SESSION 31 STOP (2026-09-21): the adapter is BUILT and proven on the 12 XOTP modules (build 5: 24 pages, means 35.6–63.1 %, every family convention verified on XOTPG04_1_0) but the round's A/B probe / scoped ship / gate suite were not run before the loop was stopped — shipped OFF so the corpus stays at the r424 proven state (2559 / 495). ENABLED 2026-09-22 (session 33 Round 1): r425 finished from the LOOP_STATE.md handover — the 12 rebuilt byte-identical to build 5, the I-can list (overview_list_after_label) added, the A/B probe over all 507 modules (OFF = disk 2559 / 2559 with the 12 refused; ON = 2583 / 2583), the FULL regeneration backstop, the 2353 -> 2377 re-base.
adapter._note: ROUND 425 (session 31 Round 3 — the spec's Round 2: the adapter, text only). DocxExtractor.AdaptActivityTable turns the activity table into the synthetic red-tag paragraph stream the whole existing pipeline already speaks (TITLE BAR / LESSON N / Lesson Overview / H2 / H3 / Body / alert / Activity / the widget invocations / button / End page), so no builder, no menu shell and no page-splitter rule is new. The mapping is DATA: the section lexicon below (left-cell text → role), the widget hints (row text → invocation tag), the page-break rule and the instruction handling. The reader book (carousel images, the picture / sentence matching payload, the acks credits) is NOT in any of the twelve documents — those widgets ship as the standard hand-off placeholders (spec §4, needs Chris: a Media List for the family).
adapter._sections_note: Tested in order against the FOLDED left cell (bold / underline markers and parenthetical notes removed, lines joined by ' / '); the first match wins; a row matching nothing is emitted as an [Activity] too (a section heading with no number — the G writers' 'Word Challenge' / 'Sequence Activity' rows carry their number on a second line, caught by the trailing-number pattern). The Quiz row and its nested 'I can' table are the D2L self-assessment quiz — never a page (spec §3.2); recorded in the run notes. The Quiz row is TERMINAL: the extractor flattens the nested 'I can' table's six rows into the outer table after it, so nothing after the Quiz row is read.
adapter._page_title_note: Every gold XOTP page's own h1 repeats the module title (XOTPG04_1_0 / _2_0: two identical `My Drum Kit` spans), so the adapted pages skip the PageSplitter heading harvest (which would take the Introduction [H2]) and the SkeletonBuilder module-title fallback applies.
adapter._no_overview_page_note: The gold's first file is 1_0 — there is no overview page; the writer's Overview row is the lesson-page module menu. The splitter's RR-4 normally merges a title-bar-only opening segment forward AS the overview (label 0.0); with this flag the segment folds into lesson 1 as a LESSON page (PageSplitter, run.noOverviewPage), so the files pair with the gold's 1_0 / 2_0 and the title still resolves from the title-bar item riding on page 1.
adapter._widget_hints_note: Matched in order over the folded text of the WHOLE row (left + right cells) — the section heading decides the widget, a CS: line only confirms it (spec §3.4: the six G / O modules carry no CS: line at all). No hint → a plain [Activity] box (Kei a koe, the Syllable Count / Word Challenge charts, whose gold is a table the writer only linked).

lines; the gold ships them as

  • on every page that has them (6 modules / 12 pages, 12 / 12) and the KB fixes the form — 01B_MODULE_MENUS_FOOTER (`
    I can:
    ` + `

overview_link_only_todo.note: Designer/Developer To Do: paste the overview from the linked Google Doc ({url}) — the Writers Template gives only its link.
overview_link_only_todo._doc: ROUND 443 (the autonomous loop's session 39 Round 5, 23 Sept 2026 — Chris's decision D13-15, Option B 'a To Do placeholder', chosen against pasting the text). XOTPB08–13's Overview cell holds 'In this module, ākonga will:' and then ONLY a link — 'Overview Set 2-Emergent' → a Google Doc — so the menu shipped the bare link label as a paragraph. An Overview line whose text is exactly a row link's label, where that link points at a Google Doc (url_match), becomes a red line carrying this note; red_flag.todo_lead renders it under the ledger's 'Designer/Developer To Do:' prefix. The XOTPG wording is NOT reused (its 'I can' goals differ). Env XOTPOVERVIEW_OFF restores the bare label.

adapter._family_note: The XOTP family's page conventions, measured over the 24 gold pages (outputs/_s31_r425_goldcensus.py): the Story-Questions alert's title is the callout's own lead (`callouts.by_tag.alert.variants` fixes it at h3 with no inner row and a col-md-9 column) and its questions are the writer's DECIMAL list (the docx numId → decimal; a table cell carries no numFmt, so the extractor marks every cell list `• ` — `questions_list: numbered` restores `1. ` and renderBlackText builds the <ol>, 11 / 12 gold); every activity box holds its content DIRECTLY (63 / 63 — `activity_box: bare` → run.activityBoxBare → activity_wrapper.open_bare); the lesson h1 repeats the module title (23 / 24 pages carry two identical `<h1><span>` — `lesson_title_repeats_module` → run.lessonTitleRepeatsModule, honoured where the registry h1_count asks for 2); a writer [H2] keeps its digit (keep_writer_digit.digits_by_prefix.2 += XOTP). Not taken: the gold's body `<h2><span>` wrapper (the corpus no_span_rule), the acks on the LAST page (the KB puts it on the overview — the first page here), the I-can items as a <ul> (plain paragraphs in the docx, the human's editorial bullets).
adapter._button_note: The Share row's 'Upload to dropbox button         Go to assessment quiz button' line: every label ends in the word 'button', so the line splits on that word and each part becomes one [button] (the r305 dropbox post-pass then adds the box's class token from the 'dropbox' label).
adapter._page_break_note: Spec §3.3: no [End page] anywhere, yet every module ships exactly two pages. Lettered labels (the G / O variant: 1A 1B 1C 2A 2B 2C) break where the lesson digit changes — derivable from the labels themselves; bare numbers (the B variant: 1 2 3 4 5) break after row 3 (verified on all six B modules). The overview row's content is repeated as each lesson page's [Lesson Overview] block — the writer's '(dropdown at top right)' is the lesson-page module menu, and the gold has no overview page.
adapter._cs_line_note: A row line opening `CS:` / `To CS:` is the writer's note to Creative Services (`CS: Create a drag and drop activity:`) — emitted as a RED span so the standard instruction path renders the Writers Note; it never becomes body prose.
adapter._parenthetical_note: A line that is wholly parenthetical — '(Answers in order: Look, seeds, …)', '(Please position the think bubble above the photo at left)' — is the writer's instruction to the developer, never page text: it is emitted as a red bracket-less span, which the normaliser classifies as an instruction and the r219 note scheme surfaces as a gate-invisible Writers Note. A 'CS:' / 'To CS:' line stays a plain paragraph: the r219 addressee-prefix scheme already renders it as a Writers Note (spec §3.4's two editorial CS: lines therefore survive as notes, exactly as the spec asks).

activity_table._note: ROUND 424 (session 31 Round 2 — the XOTP recognition round, LOOP_INTAKE 2026-09-19 §7 item 4, spec 00-NEW_NEW_NEW/_SPEC__XOTP_Activity_Table_Template.md §3.1 / §6 round 1). The twelve XOTP documents (XOTPB08–13, XOTPG01, XOTPG03–06, XOTPO01) carry NO square-bracket red tags; the structure lives in one two-column table whose header row is 'Section heading | Text/Activity' (the table opens with a merged title row, so the header is the SECOND row — scan_rows). MEASURED (outputs/_s31_r424_attable.cjs over all 762 docx): the header pair exists in exactly the 12 XOTP Writers Templates and nowhere else in the corpus, so the detector is exact and output-inert for every existing module by construction. DocxExtractor.IsActivityTableDoc reads it; ModuleResolver.PrepareRun takes such a document as the WT when the standard chain found none, and — with adapter.enabled false — returns the data-driven 'unsupported' refusal (label / action above) that batch_convert reports as 'refused by design' and the App renders in the summary, in place of the misleading 'no Writers Template (no content opener found)'. Same header test as pageforge-site/js/formatter.js OutputFormatter.ACTIVITY_TABLE_NOTICE (round 409, the parsed-text tab). Env ACTTABLE_OFF reverts to the pre-424 'no-wt' path.

phrases_contains: please supply details for all external media
media_list_preamble._forms_note: Three shapes, all measured on the r366 corpus: (1) the table in THIS document — the walk goes backwards from it; (2) no_table_heading — the WT carries the template's 'MEDIA LIST' heading + its instructions but the table is in a separate Media List docx (CHFUN01/04/05/06/07): the run is taken FORWARD from the heading and needs at least one contains-phrase after it; (3) label_max_words — a short plain label the writer puts on the table ('Phase 1', MXFUN03) is passed over between the preamble and the table (never above the preamble), and tail_extra_media_tables drops a SECOND media table that follows the first with only labels / blanks between (the same column test MediaListParser uses).
media_list_preamble._tail_note: The template's SUBMISSION CHECKLIST ('Have you: ☐ Completed Section A …') follows the media table on 81 of the 277 combined WTs and rendered as learner-facing text on 22 pages (gold 0). It is dropped with the table when the first non-blank block after the table opens with a tail_start_phrases entry AND every block to the end of the document is a paragraph carrying no red span that resolves to a tail_structural_directives tag other than [body] — the AR-5 substance test, so a media table placed mid-document (MXFUN01/02/03: Phase 2 content follows it) keeps its tail by construction. 175 combined WTs have nothing after the table; the ~20 with other trailing prose (an asset list, a stray URL) are left as they are.
media_list_preamble.rule: ROUND 370 (the autonomous loop's session 23, Round 1, 2026-09-18). In a COMBINED Writers Template + Media List docx the media-list section opens after the last content page with a red 'MEDIA LIST' heading, the red 'Please supply details for ALL external media …' instruction and a plain-text copyright-clearance bullet ('If a specific third-party item/image is crucial to your writing, then please submit this for early copyright clearance …' with its sharepoint link), then the media TABLE. Only the table was ever excluded from the content stream (ModuleResolver.PrepareRun), so the preamble flowed into the LAST LESSON PAGE: the two red runs became Writers Notes and the bullet rendered as learner-facing body text on 136 pages / 134 modules (Standard 85 / Fundamentals 27 / Inquiry 24); the human gold ships it on 0 of 2385 pages; 435 WTs carry the bullet. DocxExtractor.TrimMediaListPreamble walks BACKWARDS from the media table: a paragraph block that is blank, whose folded text (red markers stripped) equals a phrases_exact entry, or contains a phrases_contains entry, is preamble; the walk stops at the first block matching none (a writer's [End] / [body] / prose) and at max_blocks. The preamble and the table are removed together; at least one phrase hit is required (blank lines alone never trigger it). A SEPARATE Media List docx is untouched by construction (its table is not among the WT's blocks). New preamble wording = a phrase added HERE. Env MLPREAMBLE_OFF reverts to dropping the table block only.

trailing_content.rule: Content after the final [end page] containing no headings and no interactives is writer-form boilerplate (copyright checklist tables etc.) — emit nothing; record one summary note. Trailing empty tables are always discarded.
